structured_output.summary:
I made 13 web search and fetch calls. Four findings are actionable.

(1) The tree has not adopted the static-shapes lever. The Fable CIFAR-10 record recipe (fulcrumresearch e1.py) explicitly sets torch._dynamo.config.automatic_dynamic_shapes=False and compiles one static graph per resolution. This matches the loop's own untimed E045 micro-benchmark: about 1.6% (~0.086 s per trial) saved at identical math. It is a zero-accuracy-cost, FLOP-neutral candidate that should stack on the E046 tip.

(2) The same recipe replaces adaptive pooling with a custom global max pool (x.flatten(2).max(dim=2).values) to avoid slow atomic kernels. The PyTorch 2.4 docs list AdaptiveMaxPool2d backward on CUDA as nondeterministic. That makes the tip's AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) a small time lever, and a minor alternative candidate for the H4.3 nondeterminism. E036/E042 still point mainly at cuDNN.

(3) For H2.12, Fable shows that per-resolution whole-step CUDA graphs (fwd, bwd, fused SGD, orthogonalized momentum) and even a whole-run mega-graph are feasible, but it publishes no isolated timing gain. Its legitimate total gain (7.6%) is attributed mainly to progressive resizing.

(4) For H7.2.4, Turbo-Muon (AOL preconditioning) saves one NS iteration out of five. On the CIFAR-10 speedrun that gave only -0.8% time (1.359 → 1.348 s) at equal accuracy. Removing one of the tip's three iterations is a harder case, and E031 showed it costs 1.8 pp, so expect less than the 1.5% the hypothesis estimates.

Other recipe data points:
- hiverge and Fable both use bs 1536 with no per-phase batch change, which is consistent with E043 refuting large low-res batches.
- Fable's LR floor is 0.05 with a constant-floor tail of 0.375 epochs after decay, and its EMA covers only the last ~8 steps. This supports H6.5 as a plausible but untested direction.
- hiverge keeps the classifier head on SGD (lr 0.54, momentum 0.825), keeps the Muon momentum buffer in fp16, and trains the whitening bias for only the first 20% of steps.
- The only other CIFAR-100 75% speedrun found (futurebiohackers, 8.11 s on Modal A100) reports that Muon lost to SGD there. The loop's E019 already contradicts that.
- Drop-Muon (random per-step layer subsets, claimed 1.4x wall-clock on CNNs) is an untested direction, but I couldn't extract its CNN details.

findings.claim: The Fable CIFAR-10 record recipe sets torch._dynamo.config.automatic_dynamic_shapes = False (with cache_size_limit raised to 64-256). Each new input shape (resolution) is compiled as a static graph.
findings.relevance: Matches the loop's own E045 follow-up micro-benchmark (static per-size graphs saved ~0.086 s per trial, ~1.6%, at equal math), which was never applied as a scored change. It is a zero-accuracy-cost, FLOP-neutral lever and is likely to transfer to the PCIe judge. Candidate new Lvl3 under H2: apply it to the E046 tip and expect time <=4.89 s with accuracy unchanged within noise.

findings.claim: The global pool is implemented as a custom GlobalAmaxPool, x.flatten(2).max(dim=2).values, with a code comment saying it avoids slow atomic kernels. The pooling change is listed among Fable's legitimate speedups; MaxPool2d(2) is kept inside the conv groups.
findings.relevance: The tip uses AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1), whose CUDA backward uses atomic scatter. Replacing it with flatten+amax is mathematically identical and may save time, especially in the launch/overhead-bound 16 px phase (E045). It is a cheap, zero-accuracy-cost candidate.

findings.claim: In PyTorch 2.4, the following ops are listed as nondeterministic, and they raise under deterministic mode: torch.nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d and AdaptiveAvgPool2d 'when attempting to differentiate a CUDA tensor', and F.interpolate in bilinear mode when differentiated.
findings.relevance: AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) entered the lineage with progressive resizing (E006/E021), the same point where run-to-run nondeterminism appeared (A1a/SGD was bit-identical). It is a secondary candidate source for H4.3. E036 (cudnn.deterministic made seed 0 bit-identical) and E042 still point mainly to cuDNN algorithm picks. The interpolate on input data has no gradient, so it is irrelevant. A flatten+amax pool would remove this candidate at no cost.

findings.claim: Fable captures whole-training-step CUDA graphs (forward + backward + fused SGD + orthogonalized-momentum update), one per (resolution, do_norm) key, plus an optional mega-graph of the entire run with precomputed scalar schedules in CUDA tensors. The code logs replay time but quantifies no graph-vs-eager saving.
findings.relevance: Shows that H2.12.1 (CUDA-graphing the 16/24 px steps with LR as 0-d tensors and renorm as a graph-key variant) is technically feasible in a similar Muon-style recipe. It offers no evidence on the size of the gain, which the loop notes was near-neutral for the Fable record.

findings.claim: Fable's legitimate gain was 1.978 s -> 1.828 s (7.6%), attributed mainly to progressive resizing (24 -> 28 -> 32 px). CUDA graphs/kernel fusion and pooling changes are listed as contributors without isolated numbers. Other removed gains were spec-gaming: precomputing data (-0.062 s), host lottery (-0.040 s) and thermal cooldown (-0.009 s).
findings.relevance: Most of the gain came from resolution, not graphs, which is consistent with H2.12's prior being low. The precompute and cooldown gains are rule-violating here (timed prepare, no sleeps) and must not be copied.

findings.claim: Fable's schedule decays linearly over 8.5 epochs to an LR floor of 0.05 (5% of peak), then holds the floor for a 0.375-epoch tail (8.875 epochs total). The EMA starts 8 steps before decay ends, updates every 4 steps, decay 0.7. The resolution schedule is per epoch: [24,24,24,28,28,28,32,32,32]. The batch is fixed at 1536, the whitening bias trains only for the first 0.2 epoch (lr then 0), and LS is 0.09.
findings.relevance: For H6.5, a tuned Muon-style recipe uses a 0.05 floor and a short end-of-run EMA, so the floor/EMA direction is plausible, though unproven on CIFAR-100. The fixed bs 1536 with no per-phase batch change is consistent with E043 (bs 2048 in low-res phases cost 0.49 pp). The whitening-bias freeze after 20% is relevant to E051's lesson that warmup serves the SGD groups (the whitening bias shares the schedule).

findings.claim: hiverge's CIFAR-10 record: bs 1536 throughout, 7.65 epochs of steps, Muon lr 0.205, momentum 0.655, Nesterov, norm_freq=4, 3 NS steps with coefficients (3.4576, -4.7391, 2.0843), and a torch.half momentum buffer. A target weight magnitude anneals from 0.5012 to 0.0786 over training. The head is on a separate SGD (lr 0.5415, momentum 0.825), the whitening bias is trained only for the first 20% of steps, and LS is 0.09.
findings.relevance: Another tuned recipe also lands on bs 1536 with no per-phase batch change (H2.11). Its head stays on SGD, whereas the loop found head-on-Muon +0.32 pp on CIFAR-100 (E044), so the 100-way head differs. Its NS coefficients differ slightly from the tip's (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315), but E033 already closed coefficient tuning. The annealed target norm is an untested renorm variant.

findings.claim: Turbo-Muon applies AOL preconditioning, X0 * diag(sum_j |X0^T X0|_ij)^(-1/2), before Newton-Schulz. This matches the reference polar error with one fewer iteration (5 -> 4). On the CIFAR-10 94% speedrun it measured 1.359 s -> 1.348 s (-0.8%) at 94.03% vs 94.04% accuracy, and the paper claims ~3% training-time reductions on fast benchmarks overall.
findings.relevance: The measured gain on an airbench-style CIFAR run is under 1%, and it comes from removing one of five iterations. Removing one of the tip's three (2 + AOL) is much harsher, and E031 showed plain 3->2 costs 1.82 pp. This lowers the expected value of H7.2.4: even if the offline spectrum test passes, expect <=1% time saving.

findings.claim: The only public CIFAR-100 75% speedrun recipe found reaches 75.29% in 8.11 s on a Modal A100-SXM4-80GB; the organizer baseline is 75.36% in 59.30 s (ResNet9-style, width 64, 40 epochs). It reports that Muon lost to SGD at every model size and dropped it.
findings.relevance: The loop's E019/E044 already contradict this for CIFAR-100 (the Muon tip at 4.955 s is far below 8.11 s). No better external CIFAR-100 reference exists, so further gains must come from the CIFAR-10 record lineage (Fable/hiverge) or from new levers.

findings.claim: Drop-Muon updates only a random subset of layers per step on a randomized schedule, combining progressive training with Muon updates. In controlled CNN experiments it reports equal accuracy up to 1.4x faster in wall-clock time than full-network Muon. I could not extract the CNN/CIFAR details: the PDF did not parse.
findings.relevance: An untested direction for the remaining per-step Muon cost (H7.2), besides fewer steps: skip the Muon update, and possibly the backward, for some groups on some steps. Prior is low at ~250 steps and 8 epochs, because skipped updates likely cost accuracy, as reducing NS quality did (E031).

findings.claim: A critical-damping momentum schedule, mu(t) = 1 - 2*sqrt(alpha(t)), reaches 90% on CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 2.34x faster than mu=0.9 but finishes 0.46 pp lower. On CIFAR-100 the final-accuracy cost grows to -1.7 pp.
findings.relevance: Weak evidence against momentum-schedule tricks for a final-accuracy target on CIFAR-100. It is consistent with H7.1, which treats Muon momentum as closed.
